steps.name: QC, load, and build DESeq2 dataset with interaction design
steps.question: Do the 12000x17 counts.csv and 16x4 metadata.csv align into a valid 2x2 (genotype: WT/KO x treatment: vehicle/drug, n=4/cell) DESeqDataSet, and do samples pass basic QC (library size, gene detection, sample correlation/PCA)?
acceptance_criteria: Counts matrix subset to the 16 samples present in metadata.csv (report and justify handling of the 17th column if it is not a sample used in the design)
DESeqDataSet built with design = ~genotype*treatment, factor levels releveled so WT and vehicle are references
Per-sample library size, gene detection counts, and PCA/sample-correlation plot generated and low-quality outliers flagged (not silently dropped)
Low-count gene filtering applied (e.g. rowSums or rowMeans threshold) prior to DESeq2 fitting, filter criterion reported

steps.name: Fit full interaction model and extract genotype x treatment interaction term
steps.question: Which genes show a statistically significant genotype x treatment interaction (i.e., the drug effect differs between WT and KO), using the full ~genotype*treatment DESeq2 model?
acceptance_criteria: DESeq() run on the full interaction design from T1S1
Interaction coefficient (genotypeKO.treatmentdrug) extracted via results(name=...) and reported with log2FoldChange, p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value for all filtered genes
LFC shrinkage applied (apeglm or ashr) on the interaction coefficient for effect-size ranking
Significant interaction genes defined at padj < 0.05 (report count) and exported as a full results table
MA plot and volcano plot of the interaction term produced

steps.name: Stratified drug-vs-vehicle effects within WT and within KO
steps.question: What is the drug-vs-vehicle effect size and significance separately in WT samples and in KO samples, to characterize the direction and magnitude of any genotype-dependent drug response found in T1S2?
acceptance_criteria: Two contrasts extracted from the same fitted interaction model (or an equivalent combined-factor model): drug vs vehicle within WT, and drug vs vehicle within KO
Each contrast reported with shrunken log2FoldChange, p-value, padj, and significant gene counts at padj < 0.05

Direct comparison table produced showing, for genes significant in the interaction term (T1S2), their effect size and direction in each genotype stratum (e.g. drug effect present only in KO, opposite-sign effects, or WT-only response)
Overlap of WT-drug-responsive and KO-drug-responsive gene sets visualized (e.g. Venn/UpSet) alongside the interaction gene list

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of interaction and stratum-specific drug response genes
steps.question: Which biological pathways are enriched among genes with a significant genotype x treatment interaction, and among genes responding to drug specifically in KO vs specifically in WT?
acceptance_criteria: fgsea (preranked on shrunken log2FoldChange x -log10(p), or equivalent statistic) run separately for: the interaction term, WT drug-vs-vehicle, and KO drug-vs-vehicle results from T1S2/T1S3
Tested against human WikiPathways, Reactome, and MSigDB Hallmark gene sets confirmed present under /mnt/refs for Homo sapiens; report if a resource is absent rather than silently skipping
Enrichment results reported with NES, p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value; top pathways per contrast tabulated
Explicit note distinguishing pathways enriched only in the KO-specific drug response from those shared with WT, to directly address whether the drug engages different biology in KO vs WT

plan.title: 2x2 genotype x drug interaction DE + pathway analysis
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a 2x2 factorial bulk RNA-seq design (genotype: WT/KO x treatment: vehicle/drug, n=4/cell, 12000 genes x 16 samples used of 17 columns) in human brain tissue. The research question — does the drug act differently in KO than WT — is fundamentally a genotype x treatment interaction question, not a simple pairwise comparison. The plan therefore: (1) QC's and loads the counts/metadata into a DESeq2 object with an explicit ~genotype*treatment design; (2) fits the full interaction model and extracts the interaction term (genotypeKO.treatmentdrug) as the primary test of differential drug response between genotypes; (3) in parallel, computes the two simple drug-vs-vehicle effects within each genotype stratum (WT drug vs vehicle; KO drug vs vehicle) via contrasts, so the interaction can be interpreted directionally (e.g., drug effect present only in KO, or opposite direction); (4) runs shrinkage (apeglm/ashr as appropriate) and visualizes results (volcano, heatmap of interaction-significant genes, PCA); (5) submits the interaction gene list and each stratum's DE list to pathway enrichment (fgsea/clusterProfiler) against human WikiPathways, Reactome, and MSigDB Hallmark/GO/canonical sets staged locally, to characterize what biological processes underlie any differential drug response. All species-matched to Homo sapiens references confirmed present in /mnt/refs. No translational/PK/safety data is present in this dataset (no compound identity, no clinical outcomes), so no translational-safety or pkpd steps are added — this stays a mechanistic transcriptomics interaction analysis.
